_meta.disclaimer: Elite tier requirements, perks, and redemption ranges are hand-compiled general guidance, not live program terms. Loyalty programs change benefits and pricing frequently and do not offer public APIs for this data — always confirm current details on the program's official site before booking.
_meta.valuationMethod: Point valuations are rough rule-of-thumb estimates (cents per point), used only for an approximate pay-with-points-vs-cash comparison — not a guarantee of achievable value.

eliteTiers.name: Diamond
perks: Guaranteed upgrade to best available room incl. some suites

redemptionGuidance.note: Hilton uses fully dynamic, revenue-based award pricing with no published category chart. Ranges below are rough real-world estimates observed across typical properties, not official figures.

pointValuation.note: Hilton points are among the lowest-valued major currencies but earned in much larger quantities per dollar; ~0.5¢/point is a common rule-of-thumb valuation.

paymentFlexibility.notes: Points & Money available on nearly all standard rooms; no blackout dates since pricing is dynamic — availability is simply priced higher on peak dates.

eliteTiers.name: Platinum Elite
perks: Lounge access or breakfast (varies by brand)

redemptionGuidance.note: Marriott moved to fully dynamic award pricing in 2022, retiring its old category chart. Ranges below are rough real-world estimates, not official figures.

pointValuation.note: Marriott's huge hotel count and brand range keeps its points moderately valuable and flexible; ~0.7¢/point is a common rule-of-thumb valuation.

paymentFlexibility.notes: Cash + Points combos widely available; no blackout dates under dynamic pricing, though prices rise on peak dates.

eliteTiers.name: Explorist
perks: Complimentary continental breakfast or F&B credit

eliteTiers.name: Globalist
perks: Confirmed suite upgrade at booking, select properties

redemptionGuidance.note: Hyatt still publishes a true category chart (roughly Category 1-8), so nominal points-per-night are much lower than other chains — each point is simply worth more. Standard/off-peak/peak pricing within a category shifts the exact cost by season.

pointValuation.note: Hyatt points are widely considered the most valuable major hotel currency — a smaller, higher-value program with fixed category pricing; ~1.8¢/point is a common rule-of-thumb valuation.

paymentFlexibility.notes: Points + Cash covers roughly half the points cost on eligible rooms; standard/off-peak/peak categories shift pricing by season rather than true blackout dates.

redemptionGuidance.note: IHG uses a base category chart with a dynamic peak-date overlay — most nights price at the category rate, but high-demand dates can price above it. Ranges below reflect that blend.

pointValuation.note: IHG's massive Holiday Inn-driven footprint keeps points earnable in volume at a modest but steady value; ~0.6¢/point is a common rule-of-thumb valuation.

paymentFlexibility.notes: Points & Cash bookings widely available; occasional 'PointBreaks'-style promotions offer deep discounts on select properties.

eliteTiers.name: Diamond
perks: Guaranteed upgrade to best available room

redemptionGuidance.note: Wyndham keeps a simple, mostly flat category chart across its economy/midscale-heavy portfolio — one of the few chains where redemption ranges stay narrow rather than wide.

pointValuation.note: Wyndham's flat, low nightly point costs make its points punch above their nominal count; ~0.9¢/point is a common rule-of-thumb valuation.

paymentFlexibility.notes: Flat category pricing keeps redemptions simple and predictable; Go Free/Go Fast (cash+points) options available on most bookings.

redemptionGuidance.note: Choice skews budget/midscale overall (Cambria and Ascend are its highest brands, not true luxury), so its top bucket has the lowest ceiling of the 6 chains here.

pointValuation.note: Choice's budget-focused portfolio keeps per-night point costs low; ~0.6¢/point is a common rule-of-thumb valuation.

paymentFlexibility.notes: Dynamic pricing with frequent low-point redemption promos at budget/midscale properties.
